To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression levels of six microRNAs, namely miR-1-1*, miR-22*, miR-29, miR-30a, miR-26 and miR-16, can distinguish between healthy and non-treated Parkinson's disease patients, and between treated and non-treated Parkinson patients, respectively.
We identified six miRNAs that are differentially expressed in the plasma of PD patients.
we identified a set of six microRNAs differentially expressed in the blood of Parkinson's disease patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of microRNA expression patterns in blood from PD subjects.
the development of new biomarkers for Parkinson's disease (PDD).
the development of a new diagnostic tool for PD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the miRNA expression profile in PD patients can be used as an effective biomarker for the disease.
this study demonstrates that blood microRNAs are potential biomarkers for Parkinson's disease.
miR-1 and miR-22*, which are up-regulated in non-treated PD subjects, and miR-16 and miR-26*, which are upregulated in treated PD patients, can be considered as promising PD biomarkers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of miRNA in blood is associated to PD and could be used for diagnosis and treatment.
the identification of miRNA expression profiles in blood samples of Parkinson's disease (early-onset) patients could contribute to the development of new biomarkers.
we found six microRNAs in blood that could be used as potential biomarkers of Parkinson's disease, two for the early diagnosis and four for the follow-up of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the identification of miRNA biomarkers for PD can be performed using blood samples.
blood samples can provide information on miRNA expression profiles associated to the disease and that miRNAs can be useful in the identification of PD subtypes.
the expression levels of specific miRNAs can be used to discriminate between PD patients and healthy subjects.
